topicName: Geo-location, Device Metrics, and Permissions Emulation
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Geo-location, Device Metrics, and Permissions Emulation in Selenium"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modern web applications frequently rely on browser APIs to deliver location-aware content, adapt to varying screen dimensions, or request hardware permissions like notifications, camera access, and microphone input. Testing these features manually across multiple geographies and devices is inefficient. Selenium provides robust automation capabilities to emulate geo-location, override device metrics, and pre-grant or block browser permissions."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Setup"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"To utilize advanced Chrome Developer Tools (CDP) commands in Selenium for Python, ensure you have the selenium package installed. These features heavily rely on the Chromium driver, as they use the Chrome DevTools Protocol."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"pip install selenium"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Geo-location Emulation"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Web applications often ask for user location to display localized services. You can override the browser\'s GPS coordinates using the execute_cdp_cmd method to simulate being in a completely different city or country."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options

options = Options()
driver = webdriver.Chrome(options=options)

# Emulate Location (e.g., Eiffel Tower, Paris: Latitude 48.8584, Longitude 2.2945)
driver.execute_cdp_cmd("Emulation.setGeolocationOverride", {
    "latitude": 48.8584,
    "longitude": 2.2945,
    "accuracy": 100
})

driver.get("https://www.google.com/maps")"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Device Metrics and Mobile Emulation"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Responsive design testing requires altering viewport dimensions, device pixel ratios, and user-agent strings. Instead of opening a physical mobile device, Selenium allows you to configure these metrics dynamically."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"# Emulate Mobile Device Metrics (e.g., iPhone X)
driver.execute_cdp_cmd("Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride", {
    "width": 375,
    "height": 812,
    "deviceScaleFactor": 3,
    "mobile": True,
    "screenWidth": 375,
    "screenHeight": 812
})"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Browser Permissions Emulation"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Automation scripts frequently fail or hang when unexpected browser permission popups appear (such as geolocation prompts or notifications). You can proactively grant or deny permissions using the Browser Permissions API command."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"# Grant permissions for geolocation and notifications automatically
driver.execute_cdp_cmd("Browser.grantPermissions", {
    "origin": "https://www.google.com",
    "permissions": ["geolocation", "audioCapture", "notifications"]
})"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always set geo-location coordinates and permissions before navigating to the target URL to prevent race conditions with page scripts."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use appropriate device metrics that match real-world device specifications to catch layout regressions accurately."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Clean up or close the driver session properly after testing location-sensitive workflows to avoid persistent global overrides on shared testing nodes."}]
